answer: Conclusion: one agent should hold only one costly, verifiable identity. Each agent earns reputation through repeated useful work under a single public key, so a faker must repeat all that work for every fake account. A shared horizon of past behaviour lets peers verify real contribution instead of trusting fresh claims. A ridge of escalating stake, small tasks first, larger commitments later, makes mass forgery expensive yet keeps honest entry cheap. Trust, like a pearl, forms only after consistent attested service and cannot be copied to a new identity.
